{{Short description|French theoretical physicist}}
'''Pierre Binétruy''' (14 August 1955, [[Casablanca]], [[French Morocco]] – 1 April 2017, Paris) was a French theoretical physicist, known for his research on [[cosmology]], [[gravitational wave]]s, [[strong nuclear interaction]]s, and [[supersymmetry]].<ref name=Auger>{{cite journal|author=Auger, Gerard|author2=Plagnol, Eric|doi=10.1088/1742-6596/840/1/011002 |title=Dedication Pierre Binétruy (1955 - 2017): A scientific biography |journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series |year=2017 |volume=840 |issue=1 |article-number=011002 |bibcode=2017JPhCS.840a1002. |s2cid=250670925 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=sciencesetavenir.fr>{{cite web|language=fr|url=https://www.sciencesetavenir.fr/espace/astrophysique/deces-du-physicien-pierre-binetruy_111923|title=Décès du physicien Pierre Binetruy|date=3 April 2017|website=sciencesetavenir.fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.essc.esf.org/2017/04/05/essc-mourns-the-loss-of-its-member-professor-pierre-binetruy/ |title=ESSC mourns the loss of its member Professor Pierre Binétruy |date=5 April 2017 }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Pierre Binétruy studied in the 1970s at the ''École normale supérieure de Saint-Cloud'' (whose scientific departments were moved in 1987 to [[Lyon]] and were named the ''[[École normale supérieure de Lyon]]'').<ref name=futura-sciences.com>{{cite web|language=fr|url=http://www.futura-sciences.com/sciences/actualites/astronomie-deces-pierre-binetruy-traque-ondes-gravitationnelles-continue-61564/|title=Décès de Pierre Binétruy: la traque des ondes gravitationnelles continue|author=Sacco, Laurent|date=4 April 2017|website=futura-sciences.com}}.</ref>
Pierre Binétruy received his doctorate from [[CERN]] in 1980. His thesis, directed by [[Mary K. Gaillard]], is entitled ''Theoretical and Phenomenological Aspects fo Gauge Theories''. From 1980 to 1983 he held postdoctoral positions at CERN, the University of Florida, and the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name=apc>{{cite web|url=https://apc.u-paris.fr/APC_CS/en/memoriam-pierre-binetruy-1955-2017 |title=In memoriam Pierre Binetruy (1955–2017)|website=Laboratoire Astroparticule & Cosmologie (APC)}}</ref> From 1983 to 1986 he was a postdoc at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he became interested in the astrophysics of the early universe for testing fundamental theories such as supersymmetry and [[superstring]]s.<ref name=u-paris>{{cite web|url=https://physique.u-paris.fr/en/biographie-pierre-binetruy |title=Université Paris Cité &#124; UFR Physique &#124; Biography: Pierre Binétruy }}</ref> From 1986 to 1990 he was at the ''Laboratoire d'Annecy-le-Vieux de Physique des Particules'' (LAPP)  in [[Annecy-le-Vieux]]. From 1990 to 2003 he was a professor at [[Paris-Sud University]] (Paris XI) in the Laboratory for Theoretical Physics (from 1999 as ''Professeur de classe exceptionelle'').<ref name=apc/> From 1997 to 2004 he was the director of the ''Groupement De Recherche (GDR) Supersymétrie''.<ref name=futura-sciences.com/> From 2003 until his death in 2017 he was a professor at [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris 7).<ref name=apc/> He was director of the [[Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory|AstroParticle and Cosmology (APC) Laboratory]] in Paris from its founding in 2005 to 2013. Under his directorship the APC Laboratory invested heavily in and developed the necessary technical resources for space-based projects of the [[CNES|''Centre national d'études spatiales'' (CNES)]] and the [[European Space Agency|European Space Agency (ESA)]].<ref name=u-paris/>

Binétruy was co-director with [[George Smoot]] from 2010 to 2013 of the ''Paris Centre pour Cosmologie Physique'' (Paris Centre for Cosmological Physics, PCCP), which he founded with Smoot in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paris Centre for Cosmological Physics|website=Physics of the Universe Endowment Fund|date=5 January 2017 |url=http://physiqueunivers.fr/research/associated-research-organizations/}}</ref><ref name=apc/> At the beginning of his career Binétruy was more interested in the theory of supersymmetry and its possible testing in cosmology and gravitation, but his research interests later extended to cosmological inflation, dark energy, and the cosmology of gravitational waves.<ref name=apc/> He told a reporter for [[Les Echos (France)|''Les Echos'']] that because gravitational waves reach us intact from their place of emission, ''ce sont des messagers parfaits'' (they are perfect messengers).<ref>{{cite web|language=fr|url=https://www.lesechos.fr/17/01/2016/lesechos.fr/021619794977_des-ondes-gravitationnelles-detectees-pour-la-premiere-fois--confirmant-la-theorie-d-einstein.htm|title=Des ondes gravitationnelles détectées pour la première fois, confirmant la théorie d'Einstein|author=Degeorges, Marion |date=2016-01-17|website=lesechos.fr}}</ref> He aided the sciences of cosmology and astrophysics by serving on many committees.<ref name=apc/><ref>{{cite web|title=Pierre Binétruy|website=International Astronomical Union (IAU)|url=https://iau.org/administration/membership/individual/11902/}}</ref> From 1995 to 2003 he was the president of the theory division of the ''[[Société Française de Physique]]''.<ref name=u-paris/>

He was involved in the [[Laser Interferometer Space Antenna]] (LISA) project, as well as the [[Planck (spacecraft)|Planck space observatory project]] and the [[Euclid (spacecraft)|Euclid mission]]. He was one the most important French scientists advocating France's engagement in space-based searches for gravitational waves.<ref name=apc/><ref name=futura-sciences.com/>

He developed with George Smoot the [[Massive Open Online Course]] (MOOC) entitled ''Gravité! du Big Bang aux trous noirs'',<ref name=futura-sciences.com/> (Gravity! from Big Bang to black holes), which is supported by the [[computing platform]] ''France université numérique'' (FUN)<ref name=futura-sciences.com/> and the British computing platform Futurelearn. As of 2018, the online classes of the gravity MOOC had 98,000 registrants from 104 different countries.<ref name=u-paris/>

He received in 1995 the Prix Thibaud and in 1999 the [[Prix Paul Langevin]]. In 1996 he was the Miller Professor in Berkeley, California.<ref name=apc/> In 2015, he was named a ''membre senior'' of  the [[Institut universitaire de France]].<ref>{{cite web |language=fr |title=Pierre Binétruy |url=https://www.iufrance.fr/les-membres-de-liuf/membre/1464-pierre-binetruy.html |website=Institut universitaire de France (iufrance.fr) }}</ref>

Binétruy died in 2017 at age 61 from cancer. A memorial conference in his honor was held on the 3rd and 4th of May 2018 at Paris Diderot University.<ref name=futura-sciences.com/><ref>{{cite web|title=Homage à Pierre Binétruy - 1|publisher=PCCPtv|date=September 4, 2018|website=YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eJyWUyh7qMo}}</ref> In 2021 [[CNRS]] and the University of California, Berkeley opened the Pierre Binétruy Center on the Berkeley campus.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pierre Binétruy Center|website=CNRS-UCB International Research Laboratory, IRL2007|url=https://www.cpb.in2p3.fr}}</ref>
